tss-grc-backend/src/main/java/com/tss/grc/module/platform/completion/BuyerGapService.java:88-191
tss-grc-backend/src/main/java/com/tss/grc/module/platform/completion/BuyerGapService.java:219-270
tss-grc-backend/src/main/java/com/tss/grc/module/platform/completion/BuyerGapService.java:340-521

Description

BuyerGapService is explicitly described in its own Javadoc as a grab-bag ("combined backend for the three module gaps the May-2026 buyer assessment flagged"). It injects 8 repositories spanning RiskControlRepository, RiskRepository, RiskAttestationRepository (risk module), EvidenceItemRepository, EvidenceConnectorRepository (evidence module), ProcessingActivityRepository (privacy module), DsrCaseRepository (privacy_lc module), and CrisisEventRepository (bcm.cycle module), and runs raw native/JPQL against risk.risks, risk.risk_appetite_statements, and EvidenceItem. It contains 7 distinct public operations plus 6 nested record DTOs. The class admits the design is convenience-driven: "Bundled into one service because each piece is a thin orchestrator ... Splitting into three services would spread the audit-trail wiring across near-empty classes."

Root cause

Organised by delivery milestone (a buyer-assessment checklist) rather than by domain. The platform module became a dumping ground for cross-module 'completion' logic that properly belongs in the risk, evidence, privacy, and bcm services.

Evidence / proof
Constructor-injected repos at lines 60-69 cross 5 module packages. appetiteVariance() (146-191) hand-writes a native join over risk.risks + risk.risk_appetite_statements. pdpl72hSweep() (480-521) mutates bcm CrisisEvent rows. evidenceFreshnessSweep() (219-270) mutates evidence EvidenceItem rows. Class length: 548 LOC.

Real-world impact

Any change to risk, evidence, privacy, or bcm schemas can force edits to this platform-layer class; the class cannot be reasoned about or tested in isolation; module ownership is blurred so two teams touch the same file. Cross-module repo reach circumvents the per-module service layer that owns audit/event wiring.

Reproduction

Open the file; count distinct module packages in the import block (risk, evidence, privacy, privacy_lc, bcm.cycle) and the 7 public methods.

Resolution

Split into domain-aligned services living in their owning modules: move risk-control linkage + appetite variance + attestation sweep into the risk module, the evidence freshness sweep + connector registry into the evidence module, and the DSR/PDPL sweeps into privacy/bcm respectively. If a thin orchestration facade is still wanted for the scheduler, have it delegate to those services rather than owning their repositories.

    private final ProcessingActivityRepository ropa;

// privacy module:  CrossBorderTransferService, DsrSlaSweepService
// bcm module:      Pdpl72hCrisisSweepService

MediumQUAL-BCMP-004Long, high-complexity method: CrisisEventService.getActiveCrisisSummary() (114 LOC) embeds the entire multi-regulator deadline engine inline
QualityCyclomatic Complexity / Long Method▾
Location tss-grc-backend/src/main/java/com/tss/grc/module/bcm/cycle/service/CrisisEventService.java:125-238 Effort M Risk A single 114-line method computes the shortest regulatory notification deadline across five Saudi regulators (SDAIA/PDPL, NCA, SAMA Cyber, SAMA BCF, NCEMA) with ~10 nested severity/flag conditionals, then derives escalation tier, an Arabic next-action label, builds a 16-field row, and sorts with a 6-branch comparator — all in one place. High branching makes the regulator-window rules hard to test and easy to break.
tss-grc-backend/src/main/java/com/tss/grc/module/bcm/cycle/service/CrisisEventService.java:138-173
tss-grc-backend/src/main/java/com/tss/grc/module/bcm/cycle/service/CrisisEventService.java:221-236

Description

getActiveCrisisSummary() loops active crises and, per crisis, runs five branch blocks (lines 141-173) to find the earliest regulatory deadline, mixing severity thresholds (>=3, >=4), boolean flags (personalDataAffected, cyberRelated) and window constants. It then computes an escalation tier (3-way), a 6-case Arabic label switch, constructs a 16-arg row, and finally sorts via a comparator with six null-handling branches. The deadline computation is reusable domain logic (the same windows appear in RegulatorCountdownService and BuyerGapService.pdpl72hSweep) but is locked inside this view method.

Root cause

The mobile-summary view was built end-to-end in one method; the regulatory-deadline rules were never extracted into a dedicated, unit-testable component.

Evidence / proof
Method spans lines 125-238 (114 LOC, the largest in the 650-LOC file per a brace-depth scan). Branch count in the deadline block alone: 5 outer `if` + nested severity/comparison conditions ≈ cyclomatic complexity well above 15 for the method.

Real-world impact

The regulator-deadline logic is hard to test in isolation, easy to get wrong (a misplaced `isBefore` silently picks the wrong regulator/deadline), and is duplicated conceptually elsewhere. Long method hampers review and future regulator additions.

Reproduction

Open lines 125-238; count the conditional branches in 141-173 and the comparator 221-236.

Resolution

Extract a `RegulatoryDeadlineCalculator` returning `record Deadline(String regulator, LocalDateTime at)` from a `CrisisEvent`, with one unit test per regulator window. Extract `escalationTier(sev)` and `nextActionLabel(status)` helpers. Reduce getActiveCrisisSummary() to: load -> map(row) -> sort, delegating to the calculator and a named `Comparator`.

▼ Before (vulnerable)
public List<ActiveCrisisSummaryRow> getActiveCrisisSummary() {
    // ...114 lines: 5 regulator branches + tier + label switch + 16-arg row + 6-branch comparator
}
▲ After (fixed)
public List<ActiveCrisisSummaryRow> getActiveCrisisSummary() {
    return events.findActive(org()).stream()
        .map(e -> toRow(e, deadlineCalc.shortest(e)))
        .sorted(ACTIVE_CRISIS_ORDER)
        .toList();
}
// RegulatoryDeadlineCalculator.shortest(e) holds the 5-regulator logic, unit-tested.

MediumQUAL-BCMP-005DashboardStats 'open critical' / 'open high' tiles are fed total counts, and pendingTasks is hardcoded 0L
QualityCorrectness Smell / Magic Number▾
Location tss-grc-backend/src/main/java/com/tss/grc/module/dashboard/service/DashboardService.java:46-76 Effort M Risk The 15-arg DashboardStats record is constructed with positional args; positions 10/11 (openCriticalRisks/openHighRisks) are passed the SAME variables as positions 2/3 (criticalRisks/highRisks), so the 'open critical' and 'open high' dashboard tiles actually display the total critical/high counts, not the open subset. pendingTasks is hardcoded 0L. Misleading executive KPIs masquerading as real data.
tss-grc-backend/src/main/java/com/tss/grc/module/dashboard/service/DashboardService.java:74-75
tss-grc-backend/src/main/java/com/tss/grc/module/dashboard/dto/DashboardStats.java:14-19

Description

In getStats(), the DashboardStats constructor call is `new DashboardStats(total, critical, high, medium, low, open, closed, totalUsers, activeUsers, critical, high, openIncidents, complianceScore, 0L, overdueItems)`. The record fields at those positions are `openCriticalRisks` and `openHighRisks` (DashboardStats.java:14) — explicitly documented as 'Aliases used by the dashboard UI'. They are populated with the unfiltered `critical`/`high` totals, so 'open critical risks' equals 'critical risks'. `pendingTasks` (position 14) is the literal `0L`, a placeholder the DTO comment confirms ('0 until those modules are implemented'). Passing 15 positional longs with no field names is itself error-prone and is what allowed this aliasing to go unnoticed.

Root cause

A wide positional record + duplicated UI 'alias' fields encouraged copy-pasting the total values rather than querying the open subset (e.g. countByOrganisationIdAndRiskLevelAndStatus). No compiler help because every parameter is `long`.

Evidence / proof
DashboardService.java:74-75 passes `critical`/`high` twice and `0L` once. DashboardStats.java:14-19 declares openCriticalRisks, openHighRisks, openIncidents, complianceScore, pendingTasks.

Real-world impact

The dashboard reports inflated 'open critical/high' figures (closed criticals are counted as open) and a permanently-zero 'pending tasks' tile, undermining the credibility of the executive dashboard — a core selling feature.

Reproduction

Seed a CRITICAL risk in CLOSED status; call getStats(); observe openCriticalRisks == criticalRisks (closed ones included). pendingTasks is always 0.

Resolution

Either compute the real open-by-level counts (add countByOrganisationIdAndRiskLevelAndStatus finders and pass them) or remove the redundant alias fields and have the UI derive them. Replace the wide positional constructor with a builder or named-component construction so position-mismatch bugs are impossible. If pendingTasks is genuinely not yet implemented, document it as such or drop the field.

▼ Before (vulnerable)
return new DashboardStats(total, critical, high, medium, low, open, closed,
        totalUsers, activeUsers, critical, high, openIncidents, complianceScore, 0L, overdueItems);
▲ After (fixed)
long openCritical = riskRepository.countByOrganisationIdAndRiskLevelAndStatus(organisationId, "CRITICAL", "OPEN");
long openHigh     = riskRepository.countByOrganisationIdAndRiskLevelAndStatus(organisationId, "HIGH", "OPEN");
return DashboardStats.builder().totalRisks(total).criticalRisks(critical).highRisks(high)
        ...
        .openCriticalRisks(openCritical).openHighRisks(openHigh)
        .openIncidents(openIncidents).complianceScore(complianceScore)
        .pendingTasks(pendingTasks).overdueItems(overdueItems).build();
References: https://refactoring.guru/smells/long-parameter-list

tss-grc-backend/src/main/java/com/tss/grc/module/reporting/service/BoardPackService.java:320
tss-grc-backend/src/main/java/com/tss/grc/module/reporting/service/BoardPackService.java:170-176
tss-grc-backend/src/main/java/com/tss/grc/module/reporting/service/ExportService.java:191
tss-grc-backend/src/main/java/com/tss/grc/module/reporting/service/ExportService.java:219
tss-grc-backend/src/main/java/com/tss/grc/module/bcm/cycle/runtime/service/ExerciseRuntimeService.java:600-617

Description

BoardPackService.renderKris() loops KRIs computing band counts via readingRepo.findFirstByKriIdOrderByReadingAtDesc(k.getId()) (line 298), then loops the same KRIs again calling the identical finder per row (line 320) — 2N queries. ExportService.kriDashboardPdf() does the same (lines 191 and 219). ExerciseRuntimeService.summarise()/ExerciseObserverService.summarise() each fire 5 separate countByOrganisationIdAndExerciseRunIdAndStatus queries per run (Runtime 600-610).

Latest-reading lookups are done row-by-row instead of with a single grouped query; scalar counts are derived from full entity-page loads; status breakdowns use one COUNT per status instead of a GROUP BY.

BoardPackService.java:298 and :320 call the same per-KRI finder in two separate loops over the same list. ExportService.java:191 and :219 identical. BoardPackService.java:170 and :176 both call findByOrganisationId(org, PageRequest.of(0,1000)). ExerciseRuntimeService.java:602-610 issues 5 (then 3 more) count queries.

Real-world impact

Reporting endpoints scale O(2N) DB round-trips with KRI count; board-pack generation pays a double full-page risk load; run summaries issue 5+ count queries each. On large tenants these endpoints become slow and DB-chatty for no functional reason.

for (KriDefinition k : kris) { ... findFirstByKriIdOrderByReadingAtDesc(k.getId()) ... } // table loop
▲ After (fixed)
Map<Long,String> latestBand = readingRepo.latestBandByKri(org); // one grouped query
for (KriDefinition k : kris) { String band = latestBand.get(k.getId()); ... }

MediumQUAL-CP-001CyberService is a God class: 613 LOC, 10 repositories, 8 unrelated entity domains in one service
QualityGod class / Single Responsibility▾
Location tss-grc-backend/src/main/java/com/tss/grc/module/cyber/service/CyberService.java:23-613 Effort L Risk Maintainability risk: a single class owning frameworks, controls, sub-controls, assessments, vulnerabilities, exceptions, incidents, assets, evidence and action plans concentrates change risk and merge conflicts; no runtime exploit but high regression surface.
tss-grc-backend/src/main/java/com/tss/grc/module/cyber/service/CyberService.java:23-613

Description

CyberService is a single @Service spanning 613 lines that injects 10 repositories (frameworkRepo, assetRepo, controlRepo, subControlRepo, assessmentRepo, vulnerabilityRepo, exceptionRepo, incidentRepo, evidenceRepo, actionPlanRepo — lines 25-34) and provides full CRUD plus workflow methods for EIGHT distinct domain concepts (frameworks, controls, sub-controls, assessments, vulnerabilities, exceptions, incidents, assets, evidence, action plans). Each domain has its own get/getAll/save/update/delete/workflow methods. This violates the Single Responsibility Principle: there is no cohesive reason these aggregates share a class beyond living under the same module. Compare with the vuln_sla and asm sub-packages, which split each concern into its own dedicated service (AttackSurfaceAssetService, AttackSurfaceFindingService, ShadowItService).

Root cause

Module was built as one flat service before sub-package extraction (asm/, vuln_sla/, threatintel/) became the pattern. The core cyber service was never decomposed to match.

Evidence / proof
10 @final repository fields (lines 25-34); 8 domain regions each delimited by a banner comment (// Frameworks, // Controls, // Sub-Controls, // Assessments, // Vulnerabilities, // Exceptions, // Incidents, // Assets, // Evidence, // Action Plans); total 613 LOC measured with wc -l.

Real-world impact

Every cyber feature change touches one file; high merge-conflict probability across teams; harder to unit-test a single domain in isolation; the class is the largest in all 5 audited packages.

Reproduction

wc -l tss-grc-backend/src/main/java/com/tss/grc/module/cyber/service/CyberService.java -> 613. Count @final repository fields -> 10. Count region banners -> 8 domains.

Resolution

Split CyberService into per-aggregate services (CyberControlService, CyberVulnerabilityService, CyberIncidentService, CyberAssetService, CyberEvidenceService, CyberActionPlanService, CyberAssessmentService) mirroring the asm/ and vuln_sla/ sub-package convention. Keep a thin CyberDashboardService for the cross-cutting getDashboard aggregation. The controller can fan out to the new services without API changes.

    private final CyberAssetRepository assetRepo;
    private final CyberControlRepository controlRepo;
    // ... 7 more repos
    // 8 domains of CRUD + workflow in one 613-line class
}
▲ After (fixed)
@Service @RequiredArgsConstructor
public class CyberControlService { private final CyberControlRepository controlRepo; /* control CRUD */ }

@Service @RequiredArgsConstructor
public class CyberVulnerabilityService { private final VulnerabilityRepository vulnRepo; /* vuln CRUD + escalate */ }

@Service @RequiredArgsConstructor
public class CyberDashboardService { /* getDashboard aggregation only */ }

MediumQUAL-CP-003PrivacyService swallows audit and event-bus exceptions with empty catch(Exception ignored) — no logging at all
QualityError handling / swallowed exception▾
Location tss-grc-backend/src/main/java/com/tss/grc/module/privacy/service/PrivacyService.java:157-185 Effort S Risk Operational visibility risk: a failing audit-log write or failing F8 event publish on the regulator-discharge path (SDAIA breach notification) is silently dropped with zero log output, so an audit-trail gap or broken automation goes completely undetected.
tss-grc-backend/src/main/java/com/tss/grc/module/privacy/service/PrivacyService.java:163-165
tss-grc-backend/src/main/java/com/tss/grc/module/privacy/service/PrivacyService.java:183-185

Description

recordSdaiaSubmission() wraps the F7 audit write and the F8 event publish in two try blocks each ending in `} catch (Exception ignored) { // ... }`. The catch bodies contain only a comment ('Audit failures must not block the regulator-discharge path.') and discard the exception entirely — no log.warn, no log.error, no stack trace, no cause. PrivacyService does not even declare a logger (no @Slf4j on the class). The intent (do not block the discharge path) is reasonable, but silently eating the exception means a persistent audit-sink outage or a serialization failure in the event payload is invisible in production logs. This is the textbook swallowed-exception anti-pattern on a compliance-critical PDPL Article 31 code path.

Root cause

Best-effort side-effects (audit + event) were made non-fatal by catching broadly, but the author omitted any logging and the class lacks a logger.

Evidence / proof
Lines 163-165: `} catch (Exception ignored) {\n    // Audit failures must not block the regulator-discharge path.\n}` and lines 183-185: `} catch (Exception ignored) {\n    // Event-bus failure must not block the regulator-discharge path.\n}`. grep confirms PrivacyService has no @Slf4j / Logger field.

Real-world impact

A broken audit trail or non-firing BREACH_REPORTED_TO_SDAIA automation cannot be diagnosed from logs; for a regulator-facing 72-hour notification flow this defeats forensic accountability.

Reproduction

Stop the audit-log datastore and call recordSdaiaSubmission(); the breach still saves and returns 200 with no log line indicating the audit write failed.

Resolution

Add @Slf4j to the class and log at WARN with the exception inside both catch blocks: `log.warn("SDAIA audit write failed for breach {} — continuing", id, ex);`. Catch a narrower type if feasible. Keep the non-fatal behaviour but make the failure observable.

▼ Before (vulnerable)
try {
    if (auditLog != null) {
        auditLog.log("BREACH_REPORTED_TO_SDAIA", "DataBreach", saved.getId(), ...);
    }
} catch (Exception ignored) {
    // Audit failures must not block the regulator-discharge path.
}
▲ After (fixed)
try {
    if (auditLog != null) {
        auditLog.log("BREACH_REPORTED_TO_SDAIA", "DataBreach", saved.getId(), ...);
    }
} catch (Exception ex) {
    log.warn("SDAIA audit write failed for breach {} — discharge continues", id, ex);
}
References: CWE-390 Detection of Error Condition Without Action · PDPL Article 31 / Implementing Regulations Art. 40
MediumQUAL-CP-004VulnerabilitySlaController does business logic, injects a repository, and reads the user id by reflection with a swallowed exception
QualityLayering violation / SOLID▾
Location tss-grc-backend/src/main/java/com/tss/grc/module/cyber/vuln_sla/controller/VulnerabilitySlaController.java:52-193 Effort M Risk Maintainability + correctness risk: the controller bypasses the service layer to query the repository and dereferences the security principal reflectively, so an API/refactor mismatch fails silently (returns null user id) and the dashboard aggregation logic lives in the wrong layer.
tss-grc-backend/src/main/java/com/tss/grc/module/cyber/vuln_sla/controller/VulnerabilitySlaController.java:52
tss-grc-backend/src/main/java/com/tss/grc/module/cyber/vuln_sla/controller/VulnerabilitySlaController.java:160-176
tss-grc-backend/src/main/java/com/tss/grc/module/cyber/vuln_sla/controller/VulnerabilitySlaController.java:180-193

Description

Three distinct layering smells in one controller: (1) it injects VulnerabilitySlaFindingRepository directly (line 52) and the dashboard() endpoint runs seven count queries plus list calls and assembles the DashboardSnapshot itself (lines 160-176) — data-access and aggregation that belong in a service. (2) currentUserId() (lines 180-193) resolves the authenticated user's id via reflection: principal.getClass().getMethod("getId").invoke(principal), to 'avoid an extra dependency from this leaf module to the security package'. (3) that reflective call is wrapped in `catch (Exception ignored) { return null; }`, so any rename of GrcUserDetails.getId(), or a different principal type, silently yields a null actor id with no log — the remediation audit row then records by=null.

Root cause

The module avoided a compile-time dependency on the security package by reflecting on the principal, and skipped the service layer for the read-heavy dashboard endpoint.

Evidence / proof
Line 52: `private final VulnerabilitySlaFindingRepository findingRepo;` in a @RestController. Lines 161-167: seven `findingRepo.countByOrganisationIdAndStatusAndIsDeletedFalse(...)` calls in the controller. Lines 186-192: `try { var m = principal.getClass().getMethod("getId"); ... } catch (Exception ignored) { return null; }`.

Real-world impact

Renaming/refactoring the principal accessor breaks user attribution with no error; dashboard query logic cannot be unit-tested without the web layer; controller and service responsibilities are blurred.

Reproduction

grep for `findingRepo` in the controller (line 52, 161-167) and `getClass().getMethod("getId")` (line 187). Change GrcUserDetails.getId() to getUserId() and observe currentUserId() returns null silently.

Resolution

Move the dashboard aggregation into VulnerabilitySlaComputeService (or a dedicated VulnSlaDashboardService) and drop the repository from the controller. Replace the reflective principal access with a typed cast to the security module's user-details type (add the dependency — it is the platform's own security package, not an external one) or inject an existing helper; on failure log at WARN instead of silently returning null.

▼ Before (vulnerable)
private final VulnerabilitySlaFindingRepository findingRepo;
// dashboard() runs 7 count queries + list calls in the controller
private static Long currentUserId() {
    ...
    try { var m = principal.getClass().getMethod("getId"); ... }
    catch (Exception ignored) { return null; }
}
▲ After (fixed)
// controller delegates:
@GetMapping("/dashboard") public DashboardSnapshot dashboard() { return computeService.dashboardSnapshot(); }
// user id via typed accessor:
private static Long currentUserId() {
    Object p = SecurityContextHolder.getContext().getAuthentication().getPrincipal();
    return (p instanceof GrcUserDetails u) ? u.getId() : null;
}
References: Layered architecture — controllers must not access repositories · CWE-390 Detection of Error Condition Without Action

tss-grc-backend/src/main/java/com/tss/grc/module/socops/service/SocOpsScheduledSweep.java:153-387

Two related issues. (1) ERROR HANDLING: tick() wraps each tenant's full sweep in `catch (Exception ex) { log.warn("[socops sweep] org={} scan failed: {}", orgId, ex.getMessage()); }` (lines 130-131). Logging only ex.getMessage() at WARN discards the stack trace and cause, so a NullPointerException (message=null) prints '... scan failed: null' with no class, line, or origin sweep. The sibling scheduler VulnerabilitySlaScheduler does this correctly — `log.error("...", ex)` (line 69). (2) DUPLICATION: the ten private sweepX methods (sweepSecurityEventSla, sweepRegulatorResponseDue, sweepCyberInsuranceRenewals, sweepIamPrivilegedReviewsDue, sweepCryptoCertExpiry, sweepPentestRetestDue, sweepSeasonalOverlayActivated, sweepForensicsHoldDisposalDue, sweepAppsecSlaBreached, sweepDlpCriticalUnreviewed) all repeat the identical body: fetch rows, loop, `if (alreadyFired(...)) continue;`, publishEvent(DomainEvent.of(...)), markFired(...), fired++. ~12 call sites of alreadyFired confirm the repeated skeleton.

Root cause

Each trigger was added by copy-paste of the previous sweep; the common loop was never abstracted. The catch was written for brevity without considering loss of the stack trace.

Evidence / proof
Line 131: `log.warn("[socops sweep] org={} scan failed: {}", orgId, ex.getMessage());` — message only. 12 `alreadyFired(...)` call sites (lines 164,183,203,213,232,252,262,284,307,330,353,377) each in an otherwise-identical for-loop body across the 10 sweep methods.

Real-world impact

A bug in any single sweep surfaces only as 'scan failed: <message-or-null>' with no stack trace, forcing a code read to find which of 10 sweeps failed; adding/changing the dedup+publish contract requires editing 10 methods.

Reproduction

Inspect tick() lines 130-131 vs VulnerabilitySlaScheduler line 69; diff any two sweepX method bodies — only the repository call, entity type string, and payload map differ.

Resolution

(1) Change the catch to log.error with the exception object: `log.error("[socops sweep] org={} scan failed", orgId, ex);`. (2) Extract a generic helper, e.g. `<E> int sweep(String entityType, List<E> rows, Function<E,Long> idOf, Function<E,String> triggerOf, Function<E,Map<String,Object>> payloadOf)` that owns the loop/alreadyFired/publish/markFired, so each sweepX becomes one call.

▼ Before (vulnerable)
} catch (Exception ex) {
    log.warn("[socops sweep] org={} scan failed: {}", orgId, ex.getMessage());
}
// + 10 copies of the for(row) { if(alreadyFired) continue; publish; markFired; fired++; } loop
▲ After (fixed)
} catch (Exception ex) {
    log.error("[socops sweep] org={} scan failed", orgId, ex);
}
// generic sweep(...) helper invoked once per trigger
References: CWE-544 / logging without stack trace · DRY · Sibling: VulnerabilitySlaScheduler.runEscalations:68-70
MediumQUAL-DUP-003Service classes copy-paste the org()/currentUserId()/emit() tenant-and-actor helper trio instead of sharing a base service or utility
QualityCode Duplication / Maintainability▾
Location tss-grc-backend/src/main/java/com/tss/grc/module/openbanking/service/ObService.java:635-644 Effort M Risk Not a security CVE, but adjacent to a security-relevant concern: the duplicated currentUserId()/org() helpers are how tenant id and actor id are resolved for writes. 259 service<->service clones / 3,219 dup lines. If one copy diverges (e.g. fails to null-check the principal, or reads the wrong tenant source), it produces a per-module tenant/actor-resolution bug that the other modules will not exhibit — exactly the kind of subtle multi-tenant isolation defect that is hard to spot. Rated Medium for maintainability + latent isolation risk.
tss-grc-backend/src/main/java/com/tss/grc/module/openbanking/service/ObService.java:635-652
tss-grc-backend/src/main/java/com/tss/grc/module/sharia/service/ShariaService.java:672-703
tss-grc-backend/src/main/java/com/tss/grc/module/fraud/service/FraudService.java
tss-grc-backend/src/main/java/com/tss/grc/module/rrp/service/RrpService.java
tss-grc-backend/src/main/java/com/tss/grc/module/reginspect/service/RegInspectService.java
tss-grc-backend/src/main/java/com/tss/grc/module/opres/service/OpResService.java

Description

java-service <-> java-service is the third-largest Java cluster: 259 clones / 3,219 dup lines. The recurring fragment is a trio of private helpers used by virtually every write path: `private static Long org() { return TenantContext.requireOrganisationId(); }`, `private static Long currentUserId()` (reads SecurityContextHolder, null-guards, casts to GrcUserDetails, returns userId), and a `private void emit(...)`/event-recording method. The top service clone the report found (ObService.java:625-656 vs ShariaService.java:672-703, 32 lines) is exactly this helper block plus the surrounding event-emit method. Static grep shows `private static Long currentUserId()` duplicated in 18 service/controller files and `TenantContext.requireOrganisationId()` referenced in 69 files.

Root cause

There is no abstract base service or shared SecurityUtils/TenantUtils class exposing currentUserId()/org(). Each module's service was bootstrapped by copying a prior module's service, carrying the private helpers along. The helpers are declared `private static`, so they cannot be reused even by sibling services in the same module.

Evidence / proof
jscpd: service<->service = 259 clones / 3,219 dup lines. grep on tss-grc-backend/src/main/java/com/tss/grc/module: `private static Long currentUserId()` in 18 files; `TenantContext.requireOrganisationId()` in 69 files. Confirmed body in ObService.java:637-644 (Authentication auth = SecurityContextHolder...; instanceof GrcUserDetails u; return u.getUserId();) is identical to the ShariaService copy.

Real-world impact

Tenant- and actor-resolution logic is the security-critical seam of a multi-tenant GRC platform, yet it lives in ~18-69 hand-copied fragments. A divergence in any one copy (missing null check, wrong tenant accessor) is a per-module isolation or audit-attribution bug. Maintenance of the event-emit plumbing is likewise multiplied across every service.

Reproduction

1) Open ObService.java:635-644 and ShariaService.java around 672-703 — identical currentUserId()/org(). 2) grep -rl 'private static Long currentUserId()' tss-grc-backend/src/main/java/com/tss/grc/module --include=*.java | wc -l → 18. 3) grep -rl 'TenantContext.requireOrganisationId()' ... | wc -l → 69.

Resolution

Introduce a shared, package-visible utility (e.g. common/security/CurrentActor.java with `static Long userId()` and `static Long organisationId()`), or an `AbstractTenantService` base class exposing protected `org()`/`currentUserId()`/`emit(...)`. Replace the per-service private statics with calls to the shared helper. Centralising currentUserId() also gives one place to fix any future principal-type or null-handling change. Keep TenantContext as the source of truth; the utility just wraps it.

▼ Before (vulnerable)
// repeated (private static) in 18+ services
private static Long org() { return TenantContext.requireOrganisationId(); }
private static Long currentUserId() {
    Authentication auth = SecurityContextHolder.getContext().getAuthentication();
    if (auth == null || !auth.isAuthenticated()
            || !(auth.getPrincipal() instanceof GrcUserDetails u)) {
        return null;
    }
    return u.getUserId();
}
▲ After (fixed)
// common/security/CurrentActor.java  (single definition)
public final class CurrentActor {
    private CurrentActor() {}
    public static Long organisationId() { return TenantContext.requireOrganisationId(); }
    public static Long userId() {
        Authentication auth = SecurityContextHolder.getContext().getAuthentication();
        return (auth != null && auth.isAuthenticated()
                && auth.getPrincipal() instanceof GrcUserDetails u) ? u.getUserId() : null;
    }
}
// in services: CurrentActor.organisationId() / CurrentActor.userId()
References: tss-grc-backend/src/main/java/com/tss/grc/module/openbanking/service/ObService.java · tss-grc-backend/src/main/java/com/tss/grc/security/GrcUserDetails.java · audit/raw/jscpd/jscpd-report.json (statistics.formats.java, service<->service clones)

MediumQUAL-ESG-003Swallowed exceptions: NdiAuditPublisher catches Exception and discards it with no logging
QualityError handling (swallowed exception)▾
Location tss-grc-backend/src/main/java/com/tss/grc/module/ndi/audit/service/NdiAuditPublisher.java:40-60 Effort S Risk Operational risk: three write paths and currentUsername() swallow every exception with `catch (Exception ignored)` and no log statement, so audit-ledger write failures vanish silently — directly undermining the compliance value of the audit trail this class exists to populate.
tss-grc-backend/src/main/java/com/tss/grc/module/ndi/audit/service/NdiAuditPublisher.java:40
tss-grc-backend/src/main/java/com/tss/grc/module/ndi/audit/service/NdiAuditPublisher.java:49
tss-grc-backend/src/main/java/com/tss/grc/module/ndi/audit/service/NdiAuditPublisher.java:60
tss-grc-backend/src/main/java/com/tss/grc/module/ndi/audit/service/NdiAuditPublisher.java:82

Description

publishTransition (40), publish (49) and publish-with-severity (60) each wrap the repo.save in `catch (Exception ignored) { /* swallow */ }`, and currentUsername() (82) does the same. The class Javadoc claims errors are 'intentionally swallowed at warn level' (lines 19-22) but there is NO Logger field and NO warn/error call anywhere in the file — the comment is false and the failures are completely invisible.

Root cause

Deliberate decision to never let an audit failure roll back the parent op (REQUIRES_NEW propagation), but implemented as a blind swallow rather than a logged swallow; the documenting comment was never reconciled with the code.

Evidence / proof
Lines 40, 49, 60, 82 all contain `catch (Exception ignored)`. No `Logger`/`LoggerFactory` import in the file. Javadoc lines 19-22 promise 'warn level' logging that does not exist.

Real-world impact

If the audit table is unavailable, schema-drifted, or a summary exceeds a constraint, NDI compliance/maturity/submission transitions still succeed but their audit rows silently disappear — an undetectable gap in the regulatory ledger and no signal to operators.

Reproduction

Force NdiAuditEventRepository.save to throw (e.g. drop the table in a test); call any NDI transition — the operation succeeds and nothing is logged.

Resolution

Add a SLF4J Logger and log at WARN with the full exception (cause) in each catch, matching the Javadoc's stated contract; keep the swallow so the parent op is unaffected.

▼ Before (vulnerable)
} catch (Exception ignored) { /* audit failure never rolls back the parent op */ }
▲ After (fixed)
} catch (Exception ex) {
    log.warn("NDI audit write failed for {}#{} action={}: {}", entityType, entityId, action, ex.toString(), ex);
}
References: CWE-390: Detection of Error Condition Without Action · https://www.slf4j.org/

Location tss-grc-backend/src/main/java/com/tss/grc/module/sust/annex/service/ReportComposerService.java:409-487 Effort M Risk Correctness + maintainability: a bespoke recursive toJson() (lines 461-487) silently mishandles types Jackson handles (no LocalDate/BigDecimal-as-number coercion, no Map-key escaping, dates only stringified upstream) and markdownToHtml() does O(n) `out.toString()` scans per cell, while Jackson is already a project dependency injected into peer services.
tss-grc-backend/src/main/java/com/tss/grc/module/sust/annex/service/ReportComposerService.java:461-487
tss-grc-backend/src/main/java/com/tss/grc/module/sust/annex/service/ReportComposerService.java:409-450
tss-grc-backend/src/main/java/com/tss/grc/module/sust/annex/service/ReportComposerService.java:421-424

Description

toJson(Object) (461-487) is a hand-written recursive JSON encoder; the comment at 459-460 explicitly says 'pulling Jackson isn't necessary'. Meanwhile NdiSubmissionPackageService and NdiReportService inject a Spring-managed ObjectMapper for exactly this. The encoder does not escape Map keys, only escapes a subset of control characters in strings, and renders any non-Map/Iterable/Number/Boolean (e.g. LocalDate, enum) via toString() with only quote-escaping. markdownToHtml (409-450) determines table-header vs cell by calling `out.toString().endsWith(...)` inside the per-cell loop (lines 424) — re-materialising the entire growing buffer on every cell.

Root cause

Author chose a local mini-implementation over the existing Jackson bean to avoid a perceived dependency, and a string-scan heuristic over tracking parser state in a variable.

Evidence / proof
Line 459-460 comment: 'Quick JSON serializer — service is small enough that pulling Jackson isn't necessary'. Line 424: `boolean isHeader = !out.toString().endsWith("</tr>") && out.toString().endsWith("<table><tr>");` — two full-buffer scans per cell. 14 injected fields (grep -c 'private final' = 14) but no ObjectMapper.

Real-world impact

Risk of malformed JSON in exported BOARD_ESG/CMA/GHG report bundles when a value is a date/enum/Map-with-special-key; quadratic-ish HTML rendering for large GHG/evidence tables; divergence from how every other report service serialises.

Reproduction

Pass a Map whose value is a LocalDate into the JSON path (e.g. via dashboard 'overall') — it is emitted as a quoted toString, not the canonical Jackson form; build a GHG report with 1000 records and profile markdownToHtml.

Resolution

Inject the existing ObjectMapper bean and call writeValueAsString for the JSON branch; for markdownToHtml track header-state in a local boolean (firstRowOfTable) instead of scanning out.toString(). Optionally replace with a maintained Markdown library.

private static String toJson(Object v) { /* 27-line bespoke recursive encoder */ }
...
boolean isHeader = !out.toString().endsWith("</tr>") && out.toString().endsWith("<table><tr>");
▲ After (fixed)
// inject: private final ObjectMapper json;
...
return new AnnexContent(markdown, html, json.writeValueAsString(jsonMap));
// header detection: track `boolean firstRow = !inTable;` set when the table opens
References: https://github.com/FasterXML/jackson · Effective Java, Item 59: Know and use the libraries

MediumQUAL-FA-005RiskControlFindingPivotService swallows all RuntimeExceptions silently via safeList/safeOpt across 8 foreign-module repositories
QualityError Handling▾
Location tss-grc-backend/src/main/java/com/tss/grc/module/governance/pivot/service/RiskControlFindingPivotService.java:656-668 Effort S Risk Reliability/observability risk: every cross-module repository call is wrapped in a catch-all that returns an empty list/Optional with no log, so a genuine DB/mapping failure in any of the 8 source modules degrades the pivot to 'no linked controls/findings/CAPA' indistinguishably from a legitimately empty graph — silently producing wrong analytics with no trace.
tss-grc-backend/src/main/java/com/tss/grc/module/governance/pivot/service/RiskControlFindingPivotService.java:656-668

Description

`safeList(Supplier<List>)` and `safeOpt(Supplier<Optional>)` catch `RuntimeException` and return `List.of()` / `Optional.empty()` with no logging. They wrap ~15 call sites spanning RiskRepository, ControlRepository, RiskControlLinkRepository, ControlAssessmentRepository, FindingRepository, two CapaTaskRepositories, ControlTestDefinitionRepository and ControlTestRunRepository. Any exception (lazy-init, mapping error, constraint, NPE) is absorbed and the pivot reports an empty section. The `dataCompletenessPct` metric then reads as a data-quality gap rather than an error.

Root cause

Defensive 'graceful missing-link handling' (documented in the class Javadoc) was implemented as a blanket catch-all rather than as null/empty handling on the actual finder return values.

Evidence / proof
Lines 656-663: `catch (RuntimeException ex) { return Collections.emptyList(); }` — no log. Lines 665-668: `catch (RuntimeException ex) { return Optional.empty(); }` — no log. The only logged catch in the class is emitPivotEvent (516-518). parseControlCodes (425-430) likewise catches Exception and silently falls back.

Real-world impact

A real failure in any source module is invisible: the pivot returns a misleadingly-empty graph, undermining the analytics the module exists to provide, and leaving no log breadcrumb for triage.

Reproduction

Inject a repository that throws (e.g. simulate a mapping error in ccmRunRepo.findRecentForTest): ccmCoverageForControls returns zero-coverage stats with no warning logged; the pivot looks healthy.

Resolution

At minimum log at WARN with the supplier context inside safeList/safeOpt (the class already has an Slf4j logger). Better: catch only the specific 'not visible to tenant' case and let infrastructure exceptions propagate to the controller's 500 handler.

▼ Before (vulnerable)
private static <T> List<T> safeList(Supplier<List<T>> sup) {
    try {
        List<T> r = sup.get();
        return r == null ? List.of() : r;
    } catch (RuntimeException ex) {
        return Collections.emptyList();
    }
}
▲ After (fixed)
private static <T> List<T> safeList(Supplier<List<T>> sup) {
    try {
        List<T> r = sup.get();
        return r == null ? List.of() : r;
    } catch (RuntimeException ex) {
        log.warn("Pivot section lookup failed, treating as empty: {}", ex.toString());
        return Collections.emptyList();
    }
}
References: Effective Java Item 77: Don't ignore exceptions · OWASP error handling

tss-grc-backend/src/main/java/com/tss/grc/module/governance/pivot/service/RiskControlFindingPivotService.java:92-130
tss-grc-backend/src/main/java/com/tss/grc/module/governance/threelines/service/ThreeLinesService.java:97-105

Description

RiskControlFindingPivotService injects RiskRepository, ControlRepository, RiskControlLinkRepository, ControlAssessmentRepository, FindingRepository, two CapaTaskRepository beans (capa + audit_lc), ControlTestDefinitionRepository and ControlTestRunRepository — 9 repositories owned by 6 other modules — and queries their entities directly. ThreeLinesService similarly injects RiskRepository, FindingRepository, CapaTaskRepository, PolicyDocumentRepository, DsrCaseRepository and UserRepository. Both also import foreign entities (Risk, Control, Finding, CapaTask, PolicyDocument, User...). This is heavier coupling than the documented per-module repository pattern.

Root cause

The aggregation/dashboard services need cross-module data and the codebase exposes no module-level read API (query service / facade), so they bind directly to foreign repositories. The pivot class Javadoc even acknowledges 'owns no tables' and reaches into source repos.

Evidence / proof
RiskControlFindingPivotService constructor (106-130) takes 9 repositories from risk/platform.controls/audit_lc/capa/ccm. ThreeLinesService fields (97-105) take 6 repositories from risk/audit_lc/capa/policy/privacy_lc/iam. jscpd also flags governance/pivot importing across modules indirectly. The CCM coverage method even pages 100 runs per definition in a loop (351-379) — N+1 over a foreign repo.

Real-world impact

Tight compile-time coupling: a finder rename in any of 6 modules forces a governance edit; the modular boundary is not enforceable; foreign N+1 query patterns (ccmRunRepo in a per-definition loop) live outside the owning module's control.

Reproduction

Inspect imports of both services: each imports entity + repository types from 6+ sibling modules under com.tss.grc.module.*.

Resolution

Introduce read-only query facades per source module (e.g. RiskQueryService.openRisksForOrg(orgId), CcmQueryService.coverageForControls(...)) and have governance depend on those interfaces instead of foreign repositories. This restores the one-repository-layer-per-module boundary and lets each module own its query/N+1 strategy.

MediumQUAL-FA-007ScmService.orgId() silently defaults to tenant 1L on null context, diverging from the require-or-throw convention used everywhere else
QualityError Handling▾
Location tss-grc-backend/src/main/java/com/tss/grc/module/scm/service/ScmService.java:39-42 Effort S Risk Tenant-safety/consistency smell: when TenantContext is empty (e.g. a misconfigured filter, scheduler, or test) ScmService quietly behaves as if the caller were org 1 instead of failing fast — masking bugs and risking cross-tenant reads/writes, while all sibling services in scope throw via TenantContext.requireOrganisationId().
tss-grc-backend/src/main/java/com/tss/grc/module/scm/service/ScmService.java:39-42

Description

`private Long orgId() { Long id = TenantContext.getCurrentTenant(); return id != null ? id : 1L; }`. Every other service in the assigned set (ShariaService, RrpService, FraudService, OpResService, IaEngagementService, SanctionsScreeningService, SanctionsHitService) uses `TenantContext.requireOrganisationId()` which throws when the tenant is absent. ScmService instead silently falls back to organisation 1.

Root cause

An early dev convenience (so the SCM UI worked before auth wiring was complete) was never removed; it predates the requireOrganisationId convention adopted by later modules.

Evidence / proof
ScmService.java:39-42 returns 1L; contrast ShariaService.java:682 `static Long org() { return TenantContext.requireOrganisationId(); }` and OpResService.java:295 identical. ScmService is also the only in-scope module that performs NO audit.log/DomainEvent emission on any mutation — inconsistent with the F7/F8 convention every sibling follows.

Real-world impact

If the tenant filter ever fails to populate context, SCM operations execute against tenant 1's vendors/contracts silently — a latent cross-tenant data-exposure path and a debugging trap, since reads succeed instead of 401/500.

Reproduction

Clear TenantContext and call ScmService.listVendors(): it returns org-1 vendors instead of throwing, unlike ShariaService.listScholars() which throws.

Resolution

Replace the 1L fallback with TenantContext.requireOrganisationId() to fail fast and match the platform convention. Separately, add the missing F7/F8 audit/event emission for SCM mutations for consistency (track as its own item).

▼ Before (vulnerable)
private Long orgId() {
    Long id = TenantContext.getCurrentTenant();
    return id != null ? id : 1L;
}
▲ After (fixed)
private Long orgId() {
    return TenantContext.requireOrganisationId();
}

Location tss-grc-backend/src/main/java/com/tss/grc/module/attachment/service/AttachmentStorageService.java:26-113 Effort M Risk Medium maintainability risk: two near-identical file-storage implementations means security-relevant logic (extension allow-list, path-traversal guard, size cap) must be patched in two places. jscpd flags four overlapping duplicate blocks (20 + 17 + 13 + 10 lines) between these two files.

MediumQUAL-IE-004ApprovalChainInstanceService.recordAction() is a 104-LOC method with the entire state machine inlined
QualityCyclomatic complexity / Long method▾
Location tss-grc-backend/src/main/java/com/tss/grc/module/workflow/approval_chains/service/ApprovalChainInstanceService.java:203-308 Effort M Risk Medium maintainability risk: the core approval-chain state-machine transition lives in one 104-line method with many branches (terminal-status guard, step-order match, parallel-rung resolution, delegation gating, REJECTED short-circuit, APPROVED rung-satisfied advance/finalise, fall-through statuses). High branch count concentrated in a single security-relevant method makes it hard to test and easy to regress.
tss-grc-backend/src/main/java/com/tss/grc/module/workflow/approval_chains/service/ApprovalChainInstanceService.java:203-308

Description

recordAction() does, in one method: terminal-status validation (207), step-order match check (210), step rows lookup (219), actor->step resolution (230), two delegation guards (232-238), action-row persistence + audit + delegated-event (240-262), then the branching state machine for REJECTED (267-274), APPROVED-with-rung-satisfied advance-or-finalise (277-301), and the else fall-through (302-306). Each of the i.setUpdatedAt/instanceRepo.save pairs is repeated five times across the branches.

Root cause

All transition concerns (validation, persistence, audit, eventing, advancement) handled inline instead of being decomposed into helpers (validateActionable, persistAction, applyDecision).

Evidence / proof
Method spans lines 203-308 (104 LOC). instanceRepo.save(i) with a preceding i.setUpdatedAt(LocalDateTime.now()) appears at lines 271, 290, 295, 300, 305 — five duplicated save blocks within the one method.

Real-world impact

Hard to unit-test individual transitions; the repeated setUpdatedAt+save pattern invites a missed update on a new branch.

Reproduction

Open the file and count branches/LOC of recordAction; note the five repeated save sites.

Resolution

Extract: (1) a guard method validating terminal status + step order + delegation, (2) a recordActionRow(...) for persistence+audit, (3) an applyApproval(...) for the advance/finalise logic. Collapse the repeated setUpdatedAt+save into a single touch-and-save call at the end.

▼ Before (vulnerable)
@Transactional
public InstanceResponse recordAction(Long instanceId, InstanceActionRequest req) {
    // 100+ lines: guards, resolution, persist, audit, REJECTED branch, APPROVED branch, else branch
}
▲ After (fixed)
@Transactional
public InstanceResponse recordAction(Long instanceId, InstanceActionRequest req) {
    ApprovalChainInstance i = loadOrThrow(instanceId);
    validateActionable(i, req);
    ApprovalChainStep target = resolveAndValidateStep(i, req);
    recordActionRow(i, target, req);
    applyDecision(i, target, req);   // handles REJECTED / APPROVED / fall-through, single save
    return toResponse(i, org());
}
References: Single Responsibility Principle
MediumQUAL-IE-008AuthController.refresh()/login() swallow the cause in broad catch(Exception) — no log, 500 with cause lost
QualityError handling▾
Location tss-grc-backend/src/main/java/com/tss/grc/module/auth/AuthController.java:94-100 Effort S Risk Medium operability risk: when the server-side refresh-token store fails to persist/rotate, the controller returns a generic 500 but never logs the underlying exception (no logger is even present in AuthController). A real DB/store fault on the security-critical login/refresh path becomes invisible to operators, making incidents hard to diagnose.
tss-grc-backend/src/main/java/com/tss/grc/module/auth/AuthController.java:94-100
tss-grc-backend/src/main/java/com/tss/grc/module/auth/AuthController.java:173-176

Description

In login() the issuance block catches `Exception ex` (line 94) and returns a 500 body but discards `ex` entirely — it is never logged. The refresh() rotation block does the same (lines 173-176). AuthController has no Logger field at all, so these failures leave no server-side trace. 'Fail closed' (returning 500) is the correct security behaviour, but losing the cause is an error-handling defect.

Root cause

Broad catch(Exception) used to fail-closed, but without log.error("...", ex) the stack trace and cause are dropped on the floor.

Evidence / proof
Lines 94-100: `} catch (Exception ex) { ... return ResponseEntity.status(500).body(Map.of("message", "Unable to record refresh token — please retry.")); }` — `ex` is captured but never used/logged. Same pattern at 173-176. No `private static final Logger` exists in the class.

Real-world impact

Refresh-store outages or persistence errors on login/refresh are undiagnosable from logs; on-call engineers see only client-side 500s.

Reproduction

Force store.recordIssuance to throw (e.g. DB down), call POST /api/auth/login — client gets a 500 but no server log line records why.

Resolution

Add a class Logger and `log.error("refresh-token issuance/rotation failed for user {}", userId, ex);` inside both catch blocks before returning the 500. Keep the fail-closed 500 behaviour.

▼ Before (vulnerable)
} catch (Exception ex) {
    return ResponseEntity.status(500).body(Map.of(
        "message", "Unable to record refresh token — please retry."));
}
▲ After (fixed)
} catch (Exception ex) {
    log.error("Refresh-token issuance failed for user {}", principal.getUserId(), ex);
    return ResponseEntity.status(500).body(Map.of(
        "message", "Unable to record refresh token — please retry."));
}
References: Logging the cause when catching broadly
MediumQUAL-RC-002ComplianceService.getStats counts findings by status="CRITICAL" but CRITICAL is a severity — count is always 0
QualityDead code / Correctness▾
Location tss-grc-backend/src/main/java/com/tss/grc/module/compliance/service/ComplianceService.java:232-248 Effort S Risk Correctness bug surfaced as dead logic: the compliance dashboard 'critical findings' tile silently always reports zero, masking real critical findings from board reporting.
tss-grc-backend/src/main/java/com/tss/grc/module/compliance/service/ComplianceService.java:233
tss-grc-backend/src/main/java/com/tss/grc/module/compliance/entity/AuditFinding.java:26-39

Description

getStats() computes `criticalFindings = findingRepo.countByOrganisationIdAndStatus(orgId, "CRITICAL")`. On AuditFinding, `status` defaults to "OPEN" and only ever holds workflow states (OPEN/CLOSED), while CRITICAL is a value of the separate `severity` column. No finding is ever persisted with status == "CRITICAL", so this count is unconditionally 0 and is fed straight into the ComplianceStats DTO that drives the dashboard.

Root cause

Field confusion between `severity` (LOW/MEDIUM/HIGH/CRITICAL) and `status` (OPEN/CLOSED). The repository finder name `countByOrganisationIdAndStatus` did not catch the mistake because the literal compiles.

Evidence / proof
ComplianceService.java:233 `long criticalFindings = findingRepo.countByOrganisationIdAndStatus(orgId, "CRITICAL");`. AuditFinding.java:26-27 `@Column(name = "severity", nullable = false) private String severity;`; AuditFinding.java:38-39 `@Column(name = "status") private String status = "OPEN";`. There is no countByOrganisationIdAndSeverity finder being used for this.

Real-world impact

The criticalFindings KPI returned by GET compliance stats is permanently 0, hiding genuinely critical findings from operators and board packs that consume the stat.

Reproduction

Seed a finding with severity=CRITICAL, status=OPEN. Call the stats endpoint; criticalFindings returns 0 instead of 1.

Resolution

Query by severity, not status: add/use `countByOrganisationIdAndSeverity` and pass "CRITICAL". Keep openFindings on status.

▼ Before (vulnerable)
long openFindings     = findingRepo.countByOrganisationIdAndStatus(orgId, "OPEN");
long criticalFindings = findingRepo.countByOrganisationIdAndStatus(orgId, "CRITICAL");
▲ After (fixed)
long openFindings     = findingRepo.countByOrganisationIdAndStatus(orgId, "OPEN");
long criticalFindings = findingRepo.countByOrganisationIdAndSeverity(orgId, "CRITICAL");
References: CWE-561: Dead Code

RegReportingService and RegInspectService contain byte-identical private helpers: `org()` (TenantContext.requireOrganisationId), `currentUserId()` (resolve GrcUserDetails from SecurityContext), `emit(trigger,type,id,corrId,payload)` (publish DomainEvent), and a near-identical `timeline(...)` writer that constructs a *Event/*Update entity. jscpd confirms a 30-line clone between ObService.java:625-654 and RegReportingService.java:633-662, and a 19-line clone between AiLifecycleService.java:349-367 and RegInspectService.java:384-408. MediumQUAL-RC-005Campaign attestation services near-duplicated between ObligationCampaignService and VendorBcpCampaignService

Location tss-grc-backend/src/main/java/com/tss/grc/module/compliance/obligation/service/ObligationCampaignService.java:56-453 Effort L Risk Maintainability risk: the obligation attestation-campaign service (state machine, rollups, period math, reminders/escalation) is structurally cloned in the TPRM BCP campaign service; bug fixes and lifecycle changes must be mirrored.

Description

}

The magic 1000 page size silently truncates results for large tenants, and the per-framework filter (`if (fnd.getFrameworkId() == null || !fnd.getFrameworkId().equals(f.getId())) continue;`) runs the whole finding set through the loop for every framework in coverage().

}
▲ After (fixed)

for (AuditFinding f : findings) { ... }   // filtered in SQL, no 1000-row cap

MediumQUAL-TI-006QuestionnaireService hand-parses SELECT-option points from JSON with indexOf/substring instead of Jackson, swallowing parse errors
QualityError handling / Reinventing-the-wheel / Brittleness▾
Location tss-grc-backend/src/main/java/com/tss/grc/module/tprm/service/QuestionnaireService.java:359-371 Effort S Risk Correctness + maintainability: vendor questionnaire scoring (which feeds the vendor risk rating) is derived by string-scanning options_json with raw indexOf/substring and a catch-all that returns null on any failure, so malformed or differently-formatted option JSON silently scores zero/null with no signal.
tss-grc-backend/src/main/java/com/tss/grc/module/tprm/service/QuestionnaireService.java:359-371

Description

In `computeScoredPoints`, the SELECT case parses option points by searching for the quoted value in `options_json`, finding the next ':' and then walking characters that are digits/'.' to extract a number: `int colon = q.getOptionsJson().indexOf(':', i); int end = colon+1; while (end < ... && "0123456789.".indexOf(charAt(end))>=0) end++; try { return new BigDecimal(substring(colon+1,end).trim())...; } catch (Exception ex) { return null; }`. The comment even says 'Without a real JSON library reference here' — but the project uses Jackson throughout (ObjectMapper is used in the CCM runners and elsewhere).

Root cause

An ad-hoc parser was written under a false assumption that no JSON library was available, with a broad catch that masks any failure as a null score.

Evidence / proof
QuestionnaireService.java:360-370 — manual `"\"" + v + "\""` lookup, char-walk number extraction, terminating `catch (Exception ex) { return null; }`. Comment line 360-361 'Without a real JSON library reference here'.

Real-world impact

Brittle to formatting (whitespace, nested objects, the value appearing as a substring of another key). On any parse hiccup the question silently contributes a null score, skewing the vendor risk rating with no log/exception. Scoring is security/compliance-relevant.

Reproduction

Provide an options_json where the option value is a substring of another option key, or with spaces around the colon — the manual parser mis-reads or returns null while a JSON parse would be correct.

Resolution

Deserialize options_json with Jackson into Map<String,Number> (or a small DTO) once, look up the option value, and surface a clear validation error (as the SCALE_1_5/BOOLEAN branches already do) instead of returning null on parse failure.

▼ Before (vulnerable)
if (q.getOptionsJson() == null) return null;
String pattern = "\"" + v + "\"";
int i = q.getOptionsJson().indexOf(pattern);
if (i < 0) throw new IllegalArgumentException("SELECT option not found: " + v);
int colon = q.getOptionsJson().indexOf(':', i);
int end = colon + 1;
while (end < q.getOptionsJson().length() && "0123456789.".indexOf(q.getOptionsJson().charAt(end)) >= 0) end++;
try { return new BigDecimal(q.getOptionsJson().substring(colon + 1, end).trim()).setScale(2, RoundingMode.HALF_UP); }
catch (Exception ex) { return null; }
▲ After (fixed)
Map<String,BigDecimal> opts = MAPPER.readValue(q.getOptionsJson(), new TypeReference<>(){});
BigDecimal pts = opts.get(v);
if (pts == null) throw new IllegalArgumentException("SELECT option not found: " + v);
return pts.setScale(2, RoundingMode.HALF_UP);

Location tss-grc-backend/src/main/java/com/tss/grc/module/bcm/cycle/runtime/service/ExerciseRuntimeService.java:280-286 Effort S Risk On run completion, createAfterActionDraft is wrapped in `catch (RuntimeException ignored)` that logs only a generic warning with no exception object, discarding the stacktrace and cause. tss-grc-backend/src/main/java/com/tss/grc/module/bcm/cycle/runtime/service/ExerciseRuntimeService.java:280-286

Description

When a run transitions to COMPLETED, the AAR draft is created in a try/catch where the catch parameter is named `ignored` and the log statement is `log.warn("AAR draft creation for run {} failed but transition stands", saved.getId());` — the caught exception is never passed to the logger, so the cause and stacktrace are lost. The intent (don't roll back the transition for a courtesy draft) is sound, but the diagnostic is gutted.

Root cause

Catch-and-continue written for resilience but logging the exception object was omitted; the `ignored` name signals the swallow.

Evidence / proof
Lines 283-285: `} catch (RuntimeException ignored) {\n    log.warn("AAR draft creation for run {} failed but transition stands", saved.getId());\n}` — no `ignored` reference in the warn call.

Reproduction

Force an exception inside createAfterActionDraft; complete a run; observe a warn line with no stacktrace/cause.

Resolution

Log the exception object so the cause is preserved: `log.warn("AAR draft creation for run {} failed but transition stands", saved.getId(), ex);` and name the variable `ex` not `ignored`.

▼ Before (vulnerable)
            } catch (RuntimeException ignored) {
                log.warn("AAR draft creation for run {} failed but transition stands", saved.getId());
            }
▲ After (fixed)
            } catch (RuntimeException ex) {
                log.warn("AAR draft creation for run {} failed but transition stands", saved.getId(), ex);
            }

Location tss-grc-backend/src/main/java/com/tss/grc/module/reporting/service/ExportService.java:307-467 Effort S Risk Three XLSX builders wrap their entire body in catch(Exception) and rethrow a generic ExportException, conflating genuine POI/IO failures with NPEs and other programming errors. tss-grc-backend/src/main/java/com/tss/grc/module/reporting/service/ExportService.java:357-359
tss-grc-backend/src/main/java/com/tss/grc/module/reporting/service/ExportService.java:401-403

riskRegisterXlsx(), findingsXlsx(), and kriDashboardXlsx() each end with `} catch (Exception e) { throw new ExportException("Excel", "Excel generation failed", e); }`. The only checked exception in scope is IOException from writeWorkbook(); catching Exception additionally swallows the category of every RuntimeException (e.g. a NullPointerException from a malformed reading) into the same generic message. The PDF path (buildReportPdf) correctly catches only the specific DocumentException.

Defensive blanket catch added to guarantee a friendly error, at the cost of distinguishing IO failures from logic bugs.

Reproduction

Resolution

Catch only IOException around writeWorkbook (the workbook try-with-resources already handles close), and let RuntimeExceptions propagate to the GlobalExceptionHandler. If a uniform export error is required, catch IOException specifically and wrap that.

▼ Before (vulnerable)
        } catch (Exception e) {
            throw new ExportException("Excel", "Excel generation failed", e);
        }
▲ After (fixed)
        } catch (java.io.IOException e) {
            throw new ExportException("Excel", "Excel workbook write failed", e);
        }
        // RuntimeExceptions propagate to GlobalExceptionHandler

Description

guardRecommendation(from,to) (401-412) and allowedFrom(from) (414-422) both hard-code the identical transition map by state. guardRecommendation checks `Set.of(...).contains(to)` per case; allowedFrom returns the same `Set.of(...)` per case. The two must be kept byte-aligned by hand.

Root cause

Need both a boolean check and the allowed-set for the IllegalTransitionException message; instead of deriving the boolean from the set, both were written out.

Evidence / proof
Both methods list `case "PENDING_REVIEW" -> Set.of("APPROVED","REJECTED","DEFERRED")` etc. The same data appears twice (also echoed a third time in the class Javadoc at lines 57-63 and 391-399).

Real-world impact

A future transition rule change applied to only one method produces inconsistent behaviour: guard allows a transition whose error message claims it isn't allowed, or vice-versa. Classic single-source-of-truth violation.

Reproduction

Add a new allowed transition to guardRecommendation only; trigger an invalid transition; the thrown IllegalTransitionException's allowed-set (from allowedFrom) is now wrong.

Resolution

Define one `Map<String,Set<String>> ALLOWED` (as ExerciseRuntimeService already does at its ALLOWED_TRANSITIONS) and derive both the boolean and the allowed-set from it.

▼ Before (vulnerable)
private static void guardRecommendation(String from, String to) {
    boolean ok = switch (from) { case "PENDING_REVIEW" -> Set.of("APPROVED","REJECTED","DEFERRED").contains(to); ... };
}
private static Set<String> allowedFrom(String from) {
    return switch (from) { case "PENDING_REVIEW" -> Set.of("APPROVED","REJECTED","DEFERRED"); ... };
}
▲ After (fixed)
private static final Map<String,Set<String>> ALLOWED = Map.of(
    "PENDING_REVIEW", Set.of("APPROVED","REJECTED","DEFERRED"),
    "DEFERRED",       Set.of("APPROVED","REJECTED","PENDING_REVIEW"),
    "APPROVED",       Set.of("PENDING_REVIEW"),
    "REJECTED",       Set.of("PENDING_REVIEW"));
private static Set<String> allowedFrom(String f) { return ALLOWED.getOrDefault(f, Set.of()); }
private static void guardRecommendation(String f, String t) { if (!allowedFrom(f).contains(t)) throw new IllegalTransitionException(f, t, allowedFrom(f)); }

▼ Before (vulnerable)

private static String safe(String s) { return s == null ? "—" : s; }  // some return "" instead
▲ After (fixed)

public static String orDash(String s)  { return s == null ? "—" : s; }
public static String orEmpty(String s) { return s == null ? ""  : s; }
// call sites: TextFormat.orDash(name) / TextFormat.orEmpty(name)

LowQUAL-BCMP-012Reflection-based principal probing with a blanket swallow in BcpBinderService.currentUserId()
QualityError Handling / Layering▾
Location tss-grc-backend/src/main/java/com/tss/grc/module/bcm/binder/service/BcpBinderService.java:290-310 Effort S Risk currentUserId() uses reflection to call getUserId()/getId() on the security principal to avoid importing GrcUserDetails, wrapped in a catch(Exception ignored) that swallows everything. Reflection over the auth principal is fragile (breaks silently on principal-shape changes) and the swallow hides genuine failures.
tss-grc-backend/src/main/java/com/tss/grc/module/bcm/binder/service/BcpBinderService.java:290-310

Description

currentUserId() obtains the Authentication, then reflectively probes method names {"getUserId","getId"} on the principal and returns the first Long result; the whole block is inside `catch (Exception ignored) { /* never bubble up */ }`. The codebase already has a concrete `GrcUserDetails` (referenced in CLAUDE.md security notes) exposing getUserId(); reflecting to avoid the import couples this service to method-name strings that the compiler cannot verify.

Root cause

An attempt to keep the binder service decoupled from the security package for test wiring, implemented via reflection + total exception suppression rather than a small shared accessor.

Evidence / proof
Lines 298-304 reflectively invoke getter names; lines 306-308 `catch (Exception ignored) { // never bubble up — current user id is informational only }`.

Real-world impact

If the principal type changes (or a getter is renamed), the user id silently becomes null with no log, degrading audit/attribution quietly. Reflection also bypasses compile-time safety and is slower than a direct call.

Reproduction

Swap the principal to a type without getUserId/getId; call currentUserId(); it returns null with no diagnostic.

Resolution

Replace with a shared `SecurityUtils.currentUserId()` that does an `instanceof GrcUserDetails` cast (the type already exists), or inject a small `CurrentUserProvider` bean. Keep the null-on-anonymous behaviour but drop the reflection and the blanket swallow; if a defensive catch is retained, log at debug with the exception.

▼ Before (vulnerable)
try {
    Object principal = a.getPrincipal();
    for (String name : new String[]{"getUserId","getId"}) {
        try { var g = principal.getClass().getMethod(name); Object v = g.invoke(principal); if (v instanceof Long l) return l; }
        catch (NoSuchMethodException ignored) {}
    }
} catch (Exception ignored) {}
return null;
▲ After (fixed)
Object principal = a.getPrincipal();
return principal instanceof GrcUserDetails u ? u.getUserId() : null;
References: https://docs.spring.io/spring-security/reference/servlet/authentication/architecture.html

Description

createPlan(@RequestBody BcmPlan req), createProcess(@RequestBody CriticalProcess req), createBia(@RequestBody BiaRecord req), createExercise(@RequestBody BcmExercise req) (and their update counterparts) accept the JPA entity directly. The controller is marked @Deprecated (legacy surface), and the module convention elsewhere uses dedicated request/response DTOs with `@Valid`. No `@Valid` appears on these bodies, so server-side validation messages (the messages*.properties machinery) are not exercised, and client-supplied entity fields like organisationId/isDeleted/createdAt can be bound.

Root cause

Legacy CRUD controller predates the DTO convention; entities double as the API contract.

Evidence / proof
BcmController.java:69 `public BcmPlan createPlan(@RequestBody BcmPlan req)`, :128 CriticalProcess, :156 BiaRecord, :190 BcmExercise — none annotated `@Valid`; methods return the entity directly too.

Real-world impact

Tenant-owned columns are part of the bind surface (defence relies entirely on the service overwriting organisationId); response leaks internal columns; no declarative validation; API contract is coupled to the DB schema so any entity change is a breaking API change.

Reproduction

POST /api/v1/bcm/legacy-plans with a JSON body including organisationId and isDeleted; observe they bind onto the entity before the service runs.

Resolution

Introduce request/response DTOs (BcmPlanRequest/Response, etc.) with Jakarta validation and `@Valid`, mapping in the service; never accept or return @Entity at the controller boundary. Since the controller is already @Deprecated, schedule this with the documented cycle-controller migration.

▼ Before (vulnerable)

public BcmPlan createPlan(@RequestBody BcmPlan req) { return bcmService.createPlan(req); }
▲ After (fixed)
@PostMapping("/legacy-plans")
public BcmPlanResponse createPlan(@Valid @RequestBody BcmPlanRequest req) {
    return bcmService.createPlan(req);
}

Description

The updateX(id, req) methods for CyberControl, CyberSubControl, ControlAssessment, Vulnerability, VulnException, CyberIncident, CyberAsset and CyberActionPlan are byte-for-byte identical except for the entity type: load existing, copy req.setId/setOrganisationId/setExternalId/setCreatedAt from existing, setIsDeleted(false), save. Likewise the deleteX(id) methods (8 copies of load + setIsDeleted(true) + save) and the saveX(entity, orgId) methods. This is the same 'reattach detached entity' merge pattern repeated ~24 times.

Root cause

No generic base service / mapper helper for the org-scoped soft-deletable CRUD pattern that every BaseEntity child shares.

Evidence / proof
updateControl (199-207), updateSubControl (240-249), updateAssessment (282-290), updateVulnerability (354-362), updateException (411-420), updateIncident (455-463), updateAsset (508-517), updateActionPlan (586-594) all repeat: req.setId(existing.getId()); req.setOrganisationId(existing.getOrganisationId()); req.setExternalId(existing.getExternalId()); req.setCreatedAt(existing.getCreatedAt()); req.setIsDeleted(false); return repo.save(req);

Real-world impact

Any change to the merge contract (e.g. also preserving a new audit column) must be hand-applied to 8 methods; easy to miss one and create an inconsistency or a mass-assignment hole.

Reproduction

Diff updateControl against updateAsset / updateIncident in CyberService.java — only the type name and repository differ.

Resolution

Introduce a small protected generic helper, e.g. protected <T extends BaseEntity> T merge(T req, T existing, JpaRepository<T,Long> repo) that copies id/orgId/externalId/createdAt and forces isDeleted=false, or use a MapStruct mapper with @MappingTarget. Each updateX collapses to load + merge.

▼ Before (vulnerable)
@Transactional
public CyberControl updateControl(Long id, CyberControl req) {
    CyberControl existing = getControl(id);
    req.setId(existing.getId());
    req.setOrganisationId(existing.getOrganisationId());
    req.setExternalId(existing.getExternalId());
    req.setCreatedAt(existing.getCreatedAt());
    req.setIsDeleted(false);
    return controlRepo.save(req);
}
// ...repeated for 7 more entities
▲ After (fixed)
private <T extends BaseEntity> T reattach(T req, T existing) {
    req.setId(existing.getId());
    req.setOrganisationId(existing.getOrganisationId());
    req.setExternalId(existing.getExternalId());
    req.setCreatedAt(existing.getCreatedAt());
    req.setIsDeleted(false);
    return req;
}
@Transactional
public CyberControl updateControl(Long id, CyberControl req) {
    return controlRepo.save(reattach(req, getControl(id)));
}

LowQUAL-CP-006SocOpsScheduledSweep.alreadyFired runs an unbounded per-entity audit scan inside every sweep loop
QualityComplexity / inefficient algorithm▾
Location tss-grc-backend/src/main/java/com/tss/grc/module/socops/service/SocOpsScheduledSweep.java:391-399 Effort S Risk Performance risk that grows with audit-log size: dedup is implemented as a full fetch of an entity's audit rows followed by an in-memory linear scan, executed once per candidate row per sweep, per tenant, hourly.
tss-grc-backend/src/main/java/com/tss/grc/module/socops/service/SocOpsScheduledSweep.java:391-399

Description

alreadyFired() calls auditRepo.findByOrganisationIdAndEntityTypeAndEntityIdOrderByCreatedAtDesc(org, entityType, entityId) — fetching EVERY audit row ever written for that entity — and then linearly scans them in Java for a matching action_type marker. It is invoked for every candidate row in all 10 sweeps. As the audit ledger accumulates history for long-lived entities (a SecurityEvent or CyberInsurance policy may collect dozens of audit rows over time), this materializes and scans an ever-growing list to answer a boolean that the database could answer with a single exists query.

Root cause

Reused a generic audit finder instead of adding a targeted existsBy...AndActionType repository method.

Evidence / proof
Lines 393-398: `List<AuditLogEntry> rows = auditRepo.findByOrganisationIdAndEntityTypeAndEntityIdOrderByCreatedAtDesc(org, entityType, entityId); for (AuditLogEntry row : rows) { if (marker.equals(row.getActionType())) return true; } return false;` — loads all rows, scans in memory.

Real-world impact

Sweep cost scales with cumulative audit history rather than open-item count; on a large tenant the hourly sweep does N_candidates full-history fetches, increasing DB load and GC pressure over the system's lifetime.

Reproduction

Read alreadyFired (391-399); note it fetches the full ordered list then iterates, called from 12 sites inside per-row loops.

Resolution

Add a repository method `boolean existsByOrganisationIdAndEntityTypeAndEntityIdAndActionType(Long org, String type, Long id, String actionType)` and have alreadyFired delegate to it, pushing the predicate to SQL and avoiding the materialized scan.

▼ Before (vulnerable)
List<AuditLogEntry> rows = auditRepo
    .findByOrganisationIdAndEntityTypeAndEntityIdOrderByCreatedAtDesc(org, entityType, entityId);
for (AuditLogEntry row : rows) {
    if (marker.equals(row.getActionType())) return true;
}
return false;
▲ After (fixed)
return auditRepo.existsByOrganisationIdAndEntityTypeAndEntityIdAndActionType(
    org, entityType, entityId, AUDIT_PREFIX + trigger);
References: Inefficient query — fetch-then-filter vs EXISTS

LowQUAL-CP-010CyberService.getDashboard is a 73-line method performing 6 full-table loads and many stream passes inline
QualityLong method / inefficiency▾
Location tss-grc-backend/src/main/java/com/tss/grc/module/cyber/service/CyberService.java:53-126 Effort M Risk Maintainability + minor performance: a single dashboard method eagerly loads all controls, vulns, incidents, assets, action plans and evidence for the tenant and runs ~15 separate stream filter/count passes over them inline.
tss-grc-backend/src/main/java/com/tss/grc/module/cyber/service/CyberService.java:53-126

Description

getDashboard(Long) is 73 lines. It calls findAllByOrganisationId on six repositories (controls, vulns, incidents, assets, action plans, evidence — lines 57,66,74,80,85,92) to pull entire tenant tables into memory, then runs roughly fifteen separate .stream().filter(...).count() passes plus four per-framework score computations (each scoreForFramework itself streams the controls twice — lines 134-145) and three additional paged recent-N queries. The counting could largely be pushed to repository count queries; at minimum the method should be decomposed per dashboard section.

Root cause

Dashboard was assembled by loading full lists and counting in Java for expedience, in one monolithic method.

Evidence / proof
Six findAllByOrganisationId calls (lines 57,66,74,80,85,92); ~15 stream counts (lines 59-104); scoreForFramework streams controls twice per framework x4 frameworks (lines 134-145, called 109-112).

Real-world impact

On large tenants the dashboard pulls every control/vuln/incident/asset/evidence/action-plan row into memory each call; method length makes the aggregation hard to follow and to test section-by-section.

Reproduction

Read getDashboard (53-126); count repository findAll* calls (6) and stream count() passes (~15). scoreForFramework (132-147) streams the same list twice.

Resolution

Extract per-section private methods (e.g. populateControlStats, populateVulnStats) and/or replace the in-memory counts with repository count-by-status queries (countByOrganisationIdAndImplementationStatus, etc.). Compute the four framework scores in a single pass over controls rather than two passes per framework.

▼ Before (vulnerable)
public CyberDashboardDto getDashboard(Long orgId) {

    dto.setCompliantControls((int) controls.stream().filter(...).count());
    // ... 5 more findAll loads + ~15 stream counts inline, 73 lines
}
▲ After (fixed)
public CyberDashboardDto getDashboard(Long orgId) {
    CyberDashboardDto dto = new CyberDashboardDto();
    populateControlStats(dto, orgId);
    populateVulnStats(dto, orgId);
    populateIncidentStats(dto, orgId);
    ...
    return dto;
}
// each helper prefers count-by-status repo queries
